chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ḥannān ibn Sadīr, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said to me: “Ibn Shubrumah asked me, ‘What do you say regarding al-qasāmah in bloodshed?’ So I answered him with what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did.
He said: ‘What do you think—if the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله had not done this, what would the position concerning it have been?’
He said: “I said to him: As for what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did, I have already informed you of it; and as for what he did not do, I have no knowledge of it.”

key_terms.الدَّمِ: bloodshed or homicide liability in legal context
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: the legal procedure of oath-taking in a bloodshed case
key_terms.الْقَوْلُ: the legal position or ruling on a matter
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله as the source of normative sunnah (prophetic tradition)

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about al-qasāmah in bloodshed and relying on the Prophet’s practice in legal rulings?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the legal matter of al-qasāmah in cases of bloodshed and grounds the answer in the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. It also highlights restraint in legal reasoning by affirming knowledge only where there is transmitted precedent from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.
